Torsion calculator

Torsion constant, torsional stiffness, twist angle and shear stress of shafts and thin-walled sections (free warping).

How it works

A shaft loaded by a torque T twists by θ = T·L/(G·J_T). The torsion constant J_T depends strongly on the shape of the section.

Key points

  • Closed sections (tubes, boxes) are orders of magnitude stiffer in torsion than open sections (strips, I-beams, slit tubes) of the same area.
  • For a thin strip J_T ≈ w·h³/3. That is why leaf springs are compliant in torsion.
  • Maximum shear is at the outer surface of a round shaft and at the middle of the long side of a rectangle.
  • Von Mises for pure shear: σ_V = √3·τ.

Assumptions

  • Free warping (see restrained warping for clamped leaf springs)
  • Linear elastic
